plan:
FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; no experiment executed, no results claimed)

═══════════════════════════════════════════
1. RESEARCH QUESTION AND HYPOTHESES
═══════════════════════════════════════════
RQ: Does the adversarial game setup in SPAG (Adversarial Taboo self-play with imitation learning of a strong teacher) yield superior reasoning improvements compared to non-adversarial game setups (20-Question and Guess-My-City) run through the same pipeline?

H1 (primary, transfer): The Adversarial-Taboo arm shows a larger gain over its no-training baseline on held-out standard reasoning benchmarks than the 20-Question and Guess-My-City arms show over theirs.
H2 (secondary, in-game): The Adversarial-Taboo arm shows a larger gain on held-out game-instance success than the non-adversarial arms.
H0: Arm gains do not differ beyond seed-level noise.
H3 (mechanism, auxiliary): The imitation-only control improves less than any self-play arm, isolating self-play as the active ingredient.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
2. ARMS (fixed by requirements: setup_2, setup_32, setup_33)
═══════════════════════════════════════════
All arms share an identical pipeline skeleton; ONLY the game differs across the three game arms.

- A1 — Adversarial Taboo (SPAG): meta-prompt generates two-role episodes (defender must convey a target word without saying it; attacker/critic adversarially probes and flags failures). The critic explicitly attacks weaknesses and identifies inferior responses, producing preference pairs (better/worse defender behavior). Trained with a DPO-style preference optimization (EPO-style in SPAG — recollection, unverified).
- A2 — 20-Question: same meta-prompt template structure and episode volume, but the critic gives cooperative/neutral feedback (guesser asks yes/no questions; no adversarial attack objective). Preference pairs constructed with the same criterion: which response better advances cooperative success.
- A3 — Guess-My-City: same constraints; descriptive/cooperative game, neutral critic feedback.
- C1 — No-training control (base model, same checkpoints/decoding).
- C2 — Imitation-only control: teacher-generated preference data with NO self-play episodes (single-pass supervised/DPO data from the teacher), matched in pair count to the game arms. This separates imitation learning from self-play effects.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
3. CONTROLLED VARIABLES AND CONFOUND PREVENTION (explicit controls)
═══════════════════════════════════════════
Confounds and their controls:
(a) Teacher/critic quality → SAME fixed judge/critic model in all arms (default: a fixed strong open-weights model at a frozen checkpoint; GPT-4 variant see §7). The critic prompt differs only in the adversarial instruction; an identical system prompt skeleton is used. Critic identity and temperature are logged and frozen.
(b) Data volume → Matched budgets: identical number of generated episodes, extracted preference pairs, and optimizer updates across A1–A3 and C2. If one game yields fewer valid pairs per episode, keep training pairs matched by generating more episodes only up to the fixed episode cap and record the shortfall — do not silently top up.
(c) Training hyperparameters → identical optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and schedule; one shared pilot sweep on A1, then frozen for all arms (avoids per-arm tuning bias).
(d) Prompt/format leakage → no game-format text in evaluation prompts; evaluation prompts are benchmark-native.
(e) Rater bias → all free-text judging automated with the same fixed judge; judge never sees the arm label; spot-check a sample with human raters for judge-drift.
(f) Selection bias in episodes → games drawn from a shared entity/word pool split into disjoint train/held-out sets; no entity appears in both.
(g) Seed variance → ≥3 independent training seeds per arm (A1–A3, C2), same seeds across arms for paired comparison.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
4. MODELS AND EVALUATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════
Base models (ASSUMPTION — recollection of SPAG, unverified): LLaMA-2-7B-Chat and LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct; if resource-constrained, run the primary model first (Llama-3-8B-Instruct) and add the second only in the extended budget. One model is sufficient for the primary claim; the second tests generality.

Evaluation, per fixed decision (1):
- PRIMARY: transfer to held-out standard reasoning benchmarks. Proposed suite (ASSUMPTION — unverified list; substitute the paper's suite if topics provide it): 3–4 benchmarks spanning distinct reasoning types, e.g., BBH (multi-task reasoning), GSM8K (math), ARC-Challenge (science reasoning), MMLU (knowledge/reasoning). Held-out splits only; no benchmark data used anywhere in training. Decoding and prompting templates frozen across arms.
- SECONDARY: in-game held-out performance — win/success rate on held-out game instances for each arm's own game, plus a cross-game probe (A1's model evaluated on A2/A3 games) to measure generality of the trained behavior.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
5. SELF-PLAY BUDGET AND CONFIGURATIONS (per fixed decision (2))
═══════════════════════════════════════════
Iteration structure: R rounds of (episode generation → critic labeling → preference-pair extraction → DPO-style training), identical R for all arms.

PRIMARY (feasible at paper-like scale, ASSUMPTION on scale):
- R = 2 rounds; ~2,000 episodes per round per arm; target ≥2,000 preference pairs per arm; ~1,000 optimizer updates total.
- Seeds: 3 per arm. Arms trained: A1, A2, A3, C2 (4 arms × 3 seeds = 12 training runs) + 2 base models evaluated (no training).
- Cost driver: critic/teacher labeling (≈8k+ episode judgments). Estimate ~O(10⁷) teacher tokens per arm.

REDUCED-BUDGET VARIANT:
- 1 base model (Llama-3-8B-Instruct only), R = 1 round, ~800 episodes/arm, ≥800 pairs/arm, 3 seeds for A1–A3 but 1 seed for C2 (its role is directional, not the headline test).
- Sensitivity note: with R=1 and fewer pairs, absolute gains shrink and CIs widen; conclusions should be reported as "direction of effect with CI" not significance-claimed if power is low. A pre-registered minimum detectable effect (e.g., ≥2 points benchmark accuracy) should be stated; if the reduced budget's power falls below detecting that MDE, the reduced variant supports only qualitative ordering.

Budget sensitivity statement: because the true budget is unknown, the design is robust in structure (matched budgets, same controls) at any scale; what degrades with budget is statistical power and the second-model generality check, not the internal validity of the comparison.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
6. ANALYSIS PLAN
═══════════════════════════════════════════
- Per arm and seed: Δbenchmark = mean held-out benchmark accuracy(post − pre). Primary contrast: Δ(A1) − max/mean of Δ(A2), Δ(A3); report per benchmark and pooled.
- Statistics: paired comparisons across matched seeds; bootstrap CIs (10k resamples over benchmark items) plus a seed-level paired permutation test. Alpha = 0.05, Holm correction across the primary contrasts (A1 vs A2, A1 vs A3).
- Also report effect sizes and CIs (not just p-values), and per-seed spread to expose self-play variance.
- H3 check: Δ(C2) vs Δ(A1..A3) with the same procedure.
- Pre-registration of the primary endpoint (pooled benchmark delta) before any training run to prevent benchmark-shopping.
- Failure modes to report explicitly: invalid episode yield per game, preference-pair shortfall, critic rejection rates — these are evidence about whether games are comparably trainable, part of the answer, not noise to hide.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
7. JUDGE/CRITIC CONFIGURATION (per fixed decision (3))
═══════════════════════════════════════════
- CONTROLLED DEFAULT: a single fixed open-weights strong model (frozen checkpoint) as critic and imitation target in every arm, including C2. Rationale: removes API-cost uncertainty and guarantees identical teacher across arms; limitation: weaker teacher may cap imitation quality identically in all arms (does not bias the contrast).
- ALTERNATIVE (paper-faithful variant): GPT-4 as critic in all arms, if access exists. Same matched-budget controls apply. If both are run, this becomes a teacher-strength factor in a 2×3 sub-design.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
8. FEASIBILITY AND DESIGN-ONLY STATUS
═══════════════════════════════════════════
Feasibility (if ever executed): 12 fine-tuning runs of ≤8B models are modest; the binding constraint is teacher labeling volume, mitigated by the fixed-critic default. The current environment (network disabled, no GPU, no ML packages) could not execute any part of this — as required, this is a design only.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
9. ASSUMPTIONS (separate from fixed requirements)
═══════════════════════════════════════════
[ASSUMPTION] Base models LLaMA-2-7B-Chat / Llama-3-8B-Instruct reflect SPAG's setup (recollection; researcher confirmed no source support is available).
[ASSUMPTION] SPAG trains via EPO-style (DPO-family) preference optimization on GPT-4-critic-labeled self-play episodes (recollection; the design only requires "some preference optimization," so substituting the paper's exact method changes nothing structurally).
[ASSUMPTION] Benchmark list (BBH/GSM8K/ARC/MMLU) is a stand-in for the paper's suite.
[ASSUMPTION] "Non-adversarial" is operationalized as cooperative/neutral critic feedback — this is the design's operationalization, not a verified paper fact.
[ASSUMPTION] Paper-scale episode/round counts (§5 primary) are rough; the matched-budget control makes conclusions robust to their exact values.

FIXED REQUIREMENTS (from task and researcher): adversarial arm = SPAG/Adversarial Taboo; non-adversarial arms = 20-Question and Guess-My-City; matched data/training budgets across arms; no-training baseline; imitation-only control; ≥3 seeds with paired statistical comparison; explicit critic and data-volume confound controls; both transfer (primary) and in-game evaluation; primary + reduced-budget configurations; no execution or fabricated results. All satisfied as specified above.

RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTIES: exact paper benchmark list and iteration counts unverifiable (no source access); reduced-budget variant may be underpowered for significance testing; GPT-4 variant availability unknown; single-model reduced variant limits generality claims. These affect power and generality, not the internal logic of the comparison.
